Amendment to dec-6da80f2a (Harness Parity & Governance-Gate Calibration, 2026-11-16). The PM (Nikhil, human owner) reviewed the recorded decision and issued two corrections that override two of the panel's four Phase 1 conclusions. These are directives from the decision owner, not new questions for re-deliberation on whether they are right -- the panel's job in this amendment is to work out the mechanics within these corrected bounds, not to re-argue the bounds themselves.

Correction 1 -- round-robin is temporary and bounded, not open-ended per-cell. The original decision said "mandatory round-robin becomes the active sampling distribution now, with holdback-style adaptive sampling reinstated per-cell only once that cell clears its sample-size bar (>=10 observations)" -- this reads as an indefinite per-cell gate with no overall stop condition. That is corrected: round-robin is a one-time bootstrap window, hard-bounded to the first 5 x harness_count real-work dispatched tasks total (5 harnesses today -- Claude, Agy, Codex, Muse, and Grok once its quota clears -- so 25 tasks), not unbounded per-cell accumulation. Work out: how the 25-task budget is allocated across cells (evenly round-robin regardless of cell fill, or does a cell stop consuming budget once it individually clears some minimum, freeing remaining budget for other cells?); what happens to cells that still have zero or too few samples when the 25-task budget is exhausted (extend, accept sparse data, or flag for a second bounded window); and how this bootstrap window relates to the existing capability_sweep.py cadence (does the bootstrap run instead of, before, or alongside the next sweep?).

Correction 2 -- Capability-Based Task Allocation is NOT retired. The original decision said the allocation table "is to be retired as a routing authority -- demoted to advisory-only -- once round-robin is implemented in Phase 2." This is corrected: capability-based task allocation is an important tenet of synlynk and must not be retired, demoted, or made advisory-only. It remains the live routing authority, both before and after the bootstrap window. The bootstrap window's sole purpose is to refresh/validate the allocation table's entries empirically -- not to replace the mechanism of capability-based allocation with round-robin as a permanent alternative. Work out: how the bootstrap's 25 observations get folded back into the allocation table at the end of the window (automatic re-ranking under what confidence/margin gate, versus a surfaced recommendation to PM, consistent with the original 2026-08-09 holdback design's canaried-overlay-with-PM-approval mechanic that dec-6da80f2a's Q3 answer already said should be retained); and whether any currently-gated lane that gets zero samples in its share of the 25-task bootstrap (e.g., a low-traffic cell) is re-queued into the next capability_sweep.py run rather than left stale, so the sparse-cell gap this whole investigation started from doesn't just recur one bootstrap window later.

Everything else in dec-6da80f2a stands unchanged and does not need re-litigating: no role/task-type/privilege hard-pin in any harness-specific instruction file (Q2); the finding that preflight-only GOVERNS enforcement is already demonstrated insufficient, flagged for Phase 2, not fixed now (Q1); the bounded-retry-then-rotate-with-ledger-logging failure policy and the PM-reviewed-exception requirement against convenience-based reversion (Q6); the two commissioned investigations (harness-parity interactive/headless trial; instruction-file and config uniformity audit) (Q5); and the Phase 1/Phase 2 scope boundary (policy/config only this phase, no code/gate changes authorized).

Produce an amended Phase 1 decision that supersedes only the round-robin-duration and allocation-table-retirement portions of dec-6da80f2a's Decision section, leaving the rest in force as written.

[model=default; version=2.1.325 (Claude Code)]

**Analysis**

Correction 1 (bootstrap bounding): The 25-task budget should allocate evenly round-robin by default, but a cell that clears a minimum floor (I'd set this lower than the full 10-observation bar — e.g. 3-5 — since 10 per cell × 5 harnesses would require 50 slots, not 25) stops consuming further budget and its share redirects to cells still below floor. This avoids wasting rotations on a harness that's already well-sampled from Phase-0 baseline data while starving a low-traffic cell. At exhaustion (25 tasks dispatched), any cell still at zero or below-floor samples is flagged, not force-fed: accept the sparse data, log it explicitly in the amendment record, and queue that specific cell for a second bounded window (same mechanics, scoped only to the still-sparse cells, not a full new 25-task sweep) rather than silently extending the first window indefinitely — that's exactly the open-endedness the PM corrected. The bootstrap runs *before* the next regular `capability_sweep.py` cadence tick, as a one-time seed; the sweep's normal cadence resumes unmodified afterward and simply inherits whatever the bootstrap wrote into the allocation table.

Correction 2 (allocation table never retired): The bootstrap's 25 observations feed in as a surfaced recommendation to PM, not an automatic re-rank — this is consistent with the 2026-08-09 holdback design's canaried-overlay-with-PM-approval mechanic that dec-6da80f2a's Q3 already preserved. Concretely: bootstrap results get written as a proposed diff against the current allocation table, gated behind the same confidence/margin threshold the holdback canary already uses, and presented for explicit PM sign-off before it becomes live routing — the table itself never goes advisory-only at any point. Any lane left at zero/sparse samples when the window closes is automatically re-queued into the *next* `capability_sweep.py` run (not dropped), closing the exact gap that started this investigation.

**Recommendation:** Adopt both mechanics above — even-split-with-reallocation-at-floor for the 25-task budget, second bounded window for leftover sparse cells, and PM-approved canaried-diff (never auto-rank) for folding bootstrap data back into the allocation table, with automatic re-queue of sparse lanes into the next sweep. This is the minimal mechanical fix that satisfies both corrections without reopening Phase 1's settled scope.

### Analysis & Amendment Mechanics

**1. Bootstrap Budget Allocation & Cadence (Correction 1)**
The 25-task budget ($5 \times \text{harnesses}$) applies across incoming real-work dispatches using global harness-level round-robin rotation, capped at 5 executions per harness. Because incoming tasks reflect organic domain demand, individual matrix cells cannot be forced without artificially constraining real work; thus, budget is consumed per harness rather than per cell. The bootstrap operates **alongside** the existing `capability_sweep.py` cadence. When the 25-task budget is exhausted, the bootstrap window closes unconditionally—no extensions. Sparse real-work observations are accepted as-is for the production sample.

**2. Table Ingestion & Sparse-Cell Re-queuing (Correction 2)**
Capability-Based Task Allocation remains the authoritative live router before, during (outside the bootstrap holdback slice), and after the window. Upon completing the 25 tasks:
- **PM Approval & Canaried Overlay:** In alignment with the 2026-08-09 holdback architecture, live telemetry does not silently mutate routing weights. The system surfaces a differential recommendation to the PM showing proposed rank changes alongside confidence margins, requiring explicit human approval prior to updating the active routing table.
- **Sweep Bridging:** Any cell or lane receiving insufficient live samples ($<3$) is automatically re-queued into the next scheduled `capability_sweep.py` synthetic batch. This bridges the sparse-cell gap through synthetic calibration rather than leaving low-traffic lanes stale.

### Panel Position
I **endorse** this amendment. Preserving Capability-Based Task Allocation as the binding routing authority while restricting round-robin sampling to a strictly bounded 25-task bootstrap window achieves empirical calibration without compromising operational reliability. Enforcing human PM sign-off via canaried overlay and offloading sparse-cell coverage directly to `capability_sweep.py` prevents both governance drift and uncalibrated routing starvation.

The amended Phase 1 decision should define round-robin as a finite bootstrap instrument, not a replacement routing model. The window should cover exactly the first `5 × harness_count` real-work dispatches—25 tasks with Claude, Agy, Codex, Muse, and Grok once eligible. Allocation should be strict and deterministic across the relevant harness/task cells, with each eligible cell receiving its turn regardless of current fill. A cell should not surrender its slot merely because it reaches a local minimum; doing so would reintroduce traffic-weighted sampling and preserve the sparse-cell problem.

The bootstrap runs before the next scheduled `capability_sweep.py` cadence and is recorded as that sweep’s empirical input, not as a parallel permanent sampler. If a cell has no eligible real work during its turn, the unused observation is recorded as unavailable rather than fabricated or silently reassigned. At exhaustion, cells with zero or insufficient observations remain explicitly sparse and are re-queued as priority targets in the next bounded `capability_sweep.py` window. No indefinite extension is authorized by Phase 1.

Capability-Based Task Allocation remains the live routing authority throughout. The 25 observations refresh and validate its evidence; they do not authorize automatic replacement or demotion of the table. At the window’s end, the system may compute candidate re-rankings, but changes should be surfaced as a canaried overlay recommendation. Activation requires the original holdback-design confidence and margin gates plus PM approval. A gated lane with zero samples must therefore remain flagged, be carried into the next sweep, and cannot be treated as empirically disproven or silently left stale.

My position is to adopt this amendment: strict 25-task round-robin bootstrap, pre-sweep execution, explicit sparse-cell carry-forward, and PM-approved canaried updates to the still-authoritative capability allocation table. All other conclusions of dec-6da80f2a remain unchanged.

Amended Phase 1 Decision to dec-6da80f2a — supersedes only Decision § Round-Robin Duration and § Allocation Table Status. All other findings stand.

**Correction 1: Round-robin bounded bootstrap (replaces indefinite per-cell gate).**

Round-robin is not a new sampling distribution. It is a one-time bootstrap window of exactly `5 x harness_count` real-work dispatched tasks. With 5 harnesses today (Claude, Agy, Codex, Muse, Grok conditional on quota) = 25 tasks.

*Allocation:* Strict round-robin across task-type cells as defined in the capability matrix, not across harnesses. Each of the next 25 dispatches rotates to the next harness in fixed order for the next queued task-type, irrespective of cell fill. A cell that reaches `n=3` observations within the window stops consuming budget — its remaining theoretical slots are yielded to the sparsest remaining cells. This prevents a high-traffic cell from starving low-traffic cells within the hard budget.

*Exhaustion:* No automatic extension. If cells remain at 0 or <3 when task 25 completes, accept sparse data — do not hold the window open. Flag all cells with <3 samples as `underpowered/stale` in the ledger and auto-requeue exactly those cells as priority targets for the next `capability_sweep.py` run. This prevents recurrence of the sparse-cell gap.

*Cadence:* Bootstrap runs *before* — not instead of nor alongside — the next sweep. `capability_sweep.py` is deferred until task 25 is logged; the sweep then consumes the bootstrap's ledger plus its normal queue, ensuring one empirical refresh path.

**Correction 2: Capability-Based Task Allocation retained as routing authority (replaces retirement to advisory-only).**

The allocation table remains the live routing authority before, during (suspended), and after the bootstrap. Round-robin is its calibration, not its replacement. Within the window, routing is round-robin; on task 26, authority reverts to the table.

*Fold-back:* No automatic re-ranking. The 25 observations are compiled into a canaried overlay recommendation surfaced to PM for approval, consistent with the 2026-08-09 holdback design retained per Q3. Automatic promotion is gated: only cells where `n≥5` in-window *and* the top harness beats second-best by ≥1.5x interquartile margin may be auto-ranked; all others require explicit PM approval. Any lane receiving zero samples in its share is not left stale — it is re-queued into the next sweep as above and retains its pre-bootstrap ranking until validated.

Q1, Q2, Q5, Q6 and the Phase 1/2 boundary (policy/config only, no code/gate changes) remain in force.

**Position:** I concur with both corrections as directed — accept the hard-bounded 25-task bootstrap with yielding + requeue mechanics, and retention of capability-based allocation under the canaried-overlay-with-PM-approval gate. This satisfies the owner's bounds while preventing both indefinite round-robin drift and stale advisory-only decay.

synthesis:
**Decision:** The amendment to dec-6da80f2a is adopted as follows, superseding only the round-robin-duration and allocation-table-retirement portions; all other sections of dec-6da80f2a (Q1, Q2, Q5, Q6, Phase 1/2 scope boundary) remain in force unchanged.

1. **Bootstrap is a one-time, hard-bounded window of exactly 5 × harness_count real-work dispatched tasks (25 today: Claude, Agy, Codex, Muse, Grok-once-cleared).** Budget allocates round-robin across task-type cells, rotating through harnesses in fixed order, with a per-cell floor of 3 observations: once a cell reaches 3 in-window samples it stops consuming further budget, and its remaining theoretical slots are yielded to the sparsest remaining cells. This is a floor-and-yield mechanic, not Codex's strict-no-yield variant — it better serves the sparse-cell problem the investigation started from without requiring the full 10-per-cell bar (which would need 50 slots, not 25). The window runs *before* the next scheduled `capability_sweep.py` cadence tick, as that sweep's empirical seed input — the sweep is deferred until task 25 is logged, then resumes its normal cadence unmodified, inheriting whatever the bootstrap wrote.

2. **At exhaustion, no automatic extension.** Cells still at 0 or below the 3-sample floor are accepted as sparse, explicitly flagged `underpowered/stale` in the ledger, and auto-requeued as priority targets in the next `capability_sweep.py` run (not a second standalone 25-task window, and not silently dropped) — this is what closes the original sparse-cell gap rather than deferring it one cycle.

3. **Capability-Based Task Allocation remains the live, binding routing authority before, during, and after the bootstrap window** — it is never retired, demoted, or made advisory-only. Round-robin is suspended-in-scope calibration traffic for the 25 tasks only; on task 26, routing authority reverts fully to the table.

4. **Fold-back is gated, not automatic.** The 25 observations are compiled into a canaried overlay recommendation surfaced to the PM for explicit approval, per the 2026-08-09 holdback design's canaried-overlay-with-PM-approval mechanic already retained under Q3. Auto-promotion without PM sign-off is permitted only for cells meeting both a minimum-n (≥5) and a confidence/margin gate (top harness beats second-best by ≥1.5× interquartile margin); all other cells require explicit PM approval before any routing change goes live. Zero/sparse-sample lanes retain their pre-bootstrap ranking until validated in a subsequent sweep.
